items.physical_scope: Adopted classical source-free Euclidean SU(2) model on closed oriented Riemannian four-manifolds, or R4 with a specified smooth S4 extension and finite action. No Lorentzian continuation, empirical assertion or quantum construction.

items.statement:
Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, meaning that every countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function, for the specified smooth gauge-data and principal-connection constructions. Let $(X,g_X)$ be a connected, compact, oriented, finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth four-manifold without boundary, with a supplied Riemannian metric. The alternative flat-space branch is standard oriented Euclidean $M=\mathbb R^4$ together with a fixed smooth trivialization outside a ball and a specified smooth extension $(\bar P,\bar A)$ over $X=S^4$ with its unit round metric, which is conformal to the flat metric in the stereographic chart. In the compact branch set $M=X$ and $(\bar P,\bar A)=(P,A)$. The extension and its transition map are part of the field data. Finite action alone is not asserted to imply such an extension. Write $g=g_X$ in the compact branch and $g=\delta$ in the flat branch.

Fix the global structure group $G=SU(2)$, not its quotient, and let $\bar P\to X$ be a smooth right principal $SU(2)$-bundle: the right action is smooth, free, and transitive on each fibre, and local trivializations are equivariant. Its isomorphism class belongs to the model-specified set $\Sigma$ of admitted bundle sectors. In the flat branch the physical bundle is $P=\bar P|_M$. An isomorphism here is a smooth equivariant diffeomorphism over $\operatorname{id}_X$, and $\Sigma$ may be a singleton. Let $\bar\omega$ be a smooth $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued principal connection one-form satisfying $R_g^*\bar\omega=\operatorname{Ad}_{g^{-1}}\bar\omega$ and $\bar\omega(\xi_{\bar P})=\xi$, where $\xi_{\bar P}(p)=\left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_0p\exp_{SU(2)}(t\xi)$. In a local section $s_i$ of $\bar P$, write $A_i=s_i^*\bar\omega$ and $F_i=dA_i+\tfrac12[A_i\wedge A_i]$; the alternating wedge–Lie bracket is normalized by $\tfrac12[A_i\wedge A_i](Y,Z)=[A_i(Y),A_i(Z)]$. The Hodge star is determined by $\alpha\wedge *_{g_X}\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_{g_X}\,d\operatorname{vol}_{g_X}$ on two-forms, acts on the form part of $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued forms, and satisfies $*_{g_X}^2=1$ there.

Adopt, independently of any Lorentzian theory, the source-free pure Euclidean $SU(2)$ model on exactly these supplied geometric data. The representation used for normalization is the defining representation on $\mathbb C^2$; no matter fields are present. In an anti-Hermitian basis $T_a=-i\sigma_a/2$, let $\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf2}(XY)$, so $\kappa(T_a,T_b)=\delta_{ab}$. Fix a dimensionless coupling $g_{\mathrm{YM}}>0$. In natural units $c=\hbar=1$, $A_\mu$ has mass dimension one and $F_{\mu\nu}$ mass dimension two. Adopt the dimensionless action

$$S_E[A]=\frac{1}{2g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2}\int_M\kappa(F_A\wedge *_gF_A).$$

In the flat-space branch require finite action in addition to the specified smooth compactification extension. Smooth gauge transformations are equivariant bundle automorphisms covering the identity; the action is evaluated on the supplied admissible connection. Classical stationarity means vanishing first variation for smooth compactly supported adjoint-bundle-valued one-form variations preserving the supplied extension/boundary data. On a closed base every smooth variation has compact support.

This is a classical Euclidean model assumption. It neither derives a Euclidean theory by Wick rotation from a Lorentzian postulate nor asserts empirical confirmation, reflection positivity, a functional measure, gauge fixing, a convergent quantum integral, or a continuum quantum theory. The closed-manifold formulation is the explicitly adopted geometric extension of the cited flat Euclidean action; finite action alone is not claimed to prove removable singularities or compactification.

items.title: Euclidean Yang–Mills sectors and instanton interpretation

items.statement:
Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, meaning that every countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function, for the specified smooth gauge-data and principal-connection constructions. Let $(X,g_X)$ be a connected, compact, oriented, finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth four-manifold without boundary, with a supplied Riemannian metric. The alternative flat-space branch is standard oriented Euclidean $M=\mathbb R^4$ together with a fixed smooth trivialization outside a ball and a specified smooth extension $(\bar P,\bar A)$ over $X=S^4$ with its unit round metric, which is conformal to the flat metric in the stereographic chart. In the compact branch set $M=X$ and $(\bar P,\bar A)=(P,A)$. The extension and its transition map are part of the field data. Finite action alone is not asserted to imply such an extension. Write $g=g_X$ in the compact branch and $g=\delta$ in the flat branch.

Fix the global structure group $G=SU(2)$, not its quotient, and let $\bar P\to X$ be a smooth right principal $SU(2)$-bundle: the right action is smooth, free, and transitive on each fibre, and local trivializations are equivariant. Its isomorphism class belongs to the model-specified set $\Sigma$ of admitted bundle sectors. In the flat branch the physical bundle is $P=\bar P|_M$. An isomorphism here is a smooth equivariant diffeomorphism over $\operatorname{id}_X$, and $\Sigma$ may be a singleton. Let $\bar\omega$ be a smooth $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued principal connection one-form satisfying $R_g^*\bar\omega=\operatorname{Ad}_{g^{-1}}\bar\omega$ and $\bar\omega(\xi_{\bar P})=\xi$, where $\xi_{\bar P}(p)=\left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_0p\exp_{SU(2)}(t\xi)$. In a local section $s_i$ of $\bar P$, write $A_i=s_i^*\bar\omega$ and $F_i=dA_i+\tfrac12[A_i\wedge A_i]$; the alternating wedge–Lie bracket is normalized by $\tfrac12[A_i\wedge A_i](Y,Z)=[A_i(Y),A_i(Z)]$. The Hodge star is determined by $\alpha\wedge *_{g_X}\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_{g_X}\,d\operatorname{vol}_{g_X}$ on two-forms, acts on the form part of $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued forms, and satisfies $*_{g_X}^2=1$ there.

Adopt the independent Euclidean model of Independent classical Euclidean SU(2) Yang–Mills model with precisely the geometric data specified above. Its action is an explicit physical assumption and is not derived by Wick rotation from a Lorentzian model. Use anti-Hermitian defining-representation generators with $\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf2}(T_aT_b)=-\tfrac12\delta_{ab}$, the positive invariant form $\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf2}(XY)$, and a fixed dimensionless coupling $g_{\mathrm{YM}}>0$. In natural units $c=\hbar=1$, $A_\mu$ has mass dimension one, $F_{\mu\nu}$ has mass dimension two, and $S_E/\hbar$ is dimensionless. The conditional Euclidean action is

$$S_E[A]=\frac{1}{2g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2}\int_M\kappa(F_A\wedge *_gF_A).$$

In the flat-space branch admissibility also requires $S_E[A]<\infty$ on $\mathbb R^4$. Define $B_{\mathrm{top}}(X,Y)=-\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf2}(XY)=\kappa(X,Y)/2$. The mathematical charge used here is the supplied trace-normalized charge of the compactified connection,

$$\nu(\bar P,\bar A)=\frac{1}{8\pi^2}\int_X B_{\mathrm{top}}(F_{\bar A}\wedge F_{\bar A})=-\frac{1}{8\pi^2}\int_X\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf2}(F_{\bar A}\wedge F_{\bar A})=-\langle c_2(\bar E_{\mathbf2}),[X]\rangle\in\mathbb Z,$$

where $\bar E_{\mathbf2}=\bar P\times_{\mathbf2}\mathbb C^2$ and the final equality uses the supplied instanton-number definition with its full-Axiom-of-Choice and Chern–Weil hypotheses. This sign makes a positive-charge self-dual configuration satisfy $F_{\bar A}=*_{g_X}F_{\bar A}$ and a negative-charge anti-self-dual configuration satisfy $F_{\bar A}=-*_{g_X}F_{\bar A}$ on the compactified base. The charge label is not asserted to classify every connected component or every gauge orbit.

Let $\mathcal A_\nu(\Sigma)$ denote the disjoint union, over the bundle sectors in $\Sigma$, of their admissible smooth connections whose compactified charge is $\nu$. In the flat-space branch, admissible connections are required to have the specified smooth extension and finite Euclidean action.

A classical Euclidean saddle is a smooth admissible connection whose first variation of $S_E$ vanishes for every smooth compactly supported connection variation preserving the boundary data. An instanton (respectively anti-instanton) saddle is a nonzero-charge saddle satisfying the positive (respectively negative) self-duality equation. A source observable is a gauge-invariant function $O$ on the admissible connection data; gauge transformations are smooth principal-bundle automorphisms over $\operatorname{id}_M$.

The notation

$$Z_{\mathrm{formal}}(\theta;O)=\sum_{\nu}e^{i\theta\nu}\int_{\mathcal A_{\nu}(\Sigma)}\mathcal D A\;O[A]e^{-S_E[A]}$$

denotes only a formal continuum sector expression over connections, with gauge redundancy left untreated. Here $\theta$ is dimensionless and has period $2\pi$ when $\nu$ is integral. The expression defines no functional measure, gauge fixing or orbit-volume prescription, determinant, convergent integral, Hilbert-space sector, or continuum quantum field theory, and selects no finite regulator or limit.

items.title: The trivial Euclidean vacuum lies in the zero-charge sector
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; readiness escalated with the assigned page Euclidean model prerequisite unresolved.
items.statement: Let $M=S^4$ be a connected compact oriented smooth four-manifold with any smooth Riemannian metric, let $P=S^4\times SU(2)$ be the trivial principal bundle, and take the zero connection $A=0$ in its global trivialization. With the SU(2) trace and charge convention of the Euclidean Yang–Mills sector definition, this configuration has $F_A=0$, $\nu(P,A)=0$, and $S_E[A]=0$. It is a classical saddle in the trivial sector, and it is not a nonzero-charge instanton saddle.

items.statement:
Let $S^4=\{z\in\mathbb R^5:|z|=1\}$ have its unit round metric. Let $p_\infty$ be the point omitted by the north stereographic chart, let $p_0$ have north-chart coordinate $x=0$, and orient $S^4$ so $dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3\wedge dx^4>0$. In the north chart put $r^2=\sum_{\mu=1}^4(x^\mu)^2$; the metric is $4(1+r^2)^{-2}\sum_\mu(dx^\mu)^2$. In the south chart put $y=x/r^2$; the metric is $4(1+|y|^2)^{-2}\sum_\mu(dy^\mu)^2$. Define $SU(2)=\{U\in M_2(\mathbb C):U^*U=I_2,\det U=1\}$. Use the Pauli matrices $\sigma_1= egin{pmatrix}0&1\1&0\end{pmatrix}$, $\sigma_2= egin{pmatrix}0&-i\i&0\end{pmatrix}$, $\sigma_3= egin{pmatrix}1&0\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$ and anti-Hermitian generators $T_a=-i\sigma_a/2$ with $\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf2}(T_aT_b)=-	frac12\delta_{ab}$. Let $\epsilon_{ijk}$ be totally antisymmetric with $\epsilon_{123}=1$, set $\eta_{aij}=\epsilon_{aij}$, $\eta_{ai4}=\delta_{ai}$, $ ar\eta_{aij}=-\epsilon_{aij}$, and $ ar\eta_{ai4}=\delta_{ai}$ for $i,j\in\{1,2,3\}$, and extend both arrays antisymmetrically in their last two indices. For any $ho>0$, put $u(x)=(x^4I_2-i x^j\sigma_j)/r$ on the overlap, and glue two trivial right $SU(2)$ bundles with local sections satisfying $s_S=s_Nu^{-1}$. The local connection potentials are

$$A_N= rac{2\eta_{a\mu
u}x^
u}{r^2+ho^2}T_a\,dx^\mu,\qquad A_S=- rac{2ho^2 ar\eta_{a\mu
u}y^
u}{1+ho^2|y|^2}T_a\,dy^\mu.$$

On the overlap the potentials obey $A_S=\operatorname{Ad}_uA_N+u\,d(u^{-1})$, with the right-action section convention above. Use the conditional Euclidean action $S_E=(2g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2)^{-1}\int_{S^4}\kappa(F\wedge *F)$ with $\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf2}(XY)$, and the compactified charge $
u=-(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf2}(F\wedge F)$, for fixed $g_{\mathrm{YM}}>0$. For this specified smooth two-chart connection, the charge is $
u=1$, the curvature is self-dual, and $S_E=8\pi^2/g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2$; it is a classical instanton saddle. If the formal sector expression includes the dimensionless theta coupling $	heta$, the corresponding formal single-saddle factor is $e^{-8\pi^2/g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2+i	heta}$. This factor is not an evaluated continuum path integral.
